contentBlocks.text: A vending machine takes an input (your selection) and always gives the exact same output for that selection. That's the core idea behind a mathematical function, which you'll work with all week.

A function is a rule that takes an input and produces exactly one output for each input — never two different outputs for the same input. We write this as f(x), read 'f of x,' meaning 'the output of the function f when the input is x.' If f(x) = x + 3, then f(2) = 2 + 3 = 5, and f(10) = 10 + 3 = 13. Check whether this is a real function: does every input give exactly one output? Try finding f(5) and f(0) for f(x) = x + 3.
You just evaluated a real function for different inputs. Tomorrow we'll learn about slope, the rate at which a linear function's output changes.

objectives: Define a function as a rule producing exactly one output per input
Evaluate a simple function f(x) for given input values
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Introduce the vending-machine analogy for a function.
2. Introduce f(x) notation using f(x) = x + 3.
3. Work through f(2) and f(10) together.
4. Have the child find f(5) and f(0) independently.
5. Complete the worksheet.
6. Preview tomorrow's topic: slope.
differentiationTips: Struggling: read f(x) aloud as 'the output when the input is x' every time, until the notation feels natural
Ready for more: ask them to invent their own simple function rule and evaluate it for 3 different inputs
The vending-machine (or any input-always-gives-same-output) analogy is worth returning to whenever the notation feels abstract
teacherGuide.answerKey: 1. f(5) = 5 + 3 = 8. 2. f(0) = 0 + 3 = 3. 3. A function gives exactly one output for each input.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses Common Core Grade 8 Functions standard 8.F.1: understanding that a function assigns exactly one output to each input, the foundational Grade 8 Functions standard this week's unit builds from.
